newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: British Airways staff hurt in Zambia riot.
newsitem.headline: British Airways staff hurt in Zambia riot.

text.p: Seventeen British Airways crew members were injured, some seriously, when rioting University of Zambia students attacked their bus with stones at the weekend, Zambian police said on Monday.
Four of the injured had to be flown to South Africa for specialist treatment, police said, adding they were unable to give details of their injuries.
Lusaka police said the cause of the disturbance, in which students indiscriminately attacked vehicles on a road parallel to their campus, had not yet been established.
"The students blocked the road and started stoning vehicles on Saturday night," police said. "We are investigating the matter to establish what led to the riot".
Student leaders said however the protest was sparked by a hit-and-run road accident in which a student suffered a broken leg.
They dispelled speculation that the violence was politically motivated, saying there was no connection between the riot and an opposition meeting on the campus earlier in the day.
"This should not be linked to politics. It was in reaction to the accident in which our colleague was injured," a student spokesman said.
